question.text: A body travels in a straight line along the x-axis. When t = 0 s, the location of the body is x = −4 m. The velocity of the body varies with time according to v = 8 − 2t, with v given in m/s and t in s.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: How many distinct instances does the body find itself 8 m away from the origin?

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Determine the exact values of time at which these occurrences take place.

conditions: initial position x = −4 m at t = 0
velocity v = 8 − 2t with v in m/s and t in s

figure.description: A schematic showing the x-axis with marks at −8 m, −4 m, 0 m, and +8 m. At t = 0, the object starts at x = −4 m with a rightward velocity of 8 m/s and a constant leftward acceleration of 2 m/s². The trajectory illustrates the object moving rightward across x = +8 m at time t₁, halting at v = 0, reversing direction to pass x = +8 m again at time t₂, and eventually reaching x = −8 m at time t₃.

solution.approach: Integrate the velocity equation to get x(t), then solve x = 8 and x = −8 separately, keeping only the positive-time roots.

steps.text: Integrate the given velocity to get the x-coordinate, using x = −4 m at t = 0.
Set x(t) = 8 and solve the quadratic for t.
Set x(t) = −8 and solve the quadratic for t, keeping only the positive root.
steps.equation: −4+8t−t² = −8 → t²−8t−4=0 → t = 4+2√5 ≈ 8.47 s (the other root is negative)

steps.text: Count all the positive times found: the particle is at a distance of 8 m from the origin three times.

common_mistakes.text: Discarding the negative-x case x = −8 entirely and reporting only 2 times, missing that the particle turns back and passes x = −8 later.
Keeping the negative root t = 4−2√5 ≈ −0.47 s from the x = −8 case as a valid time, which is not physical since t must be positive.
